name: Two pointers
intuition: Two indices move through a sequence so that every step rules out candidates for good.

variants.name: Opposite ends
variants.summary: Start at both ends and move inward, dropping one end per step.
variants.requires: A rule that proves one end can be dropped safely, usually sorted order or a mirror comparison.

variants.name: Same direction
variants.summary: A slow and a fast index move left to right, such as compacting an array in place.
variants.requires: Everything behind the slow index is already final and never needs another look.

variants.name: Merge two sorted inputs
variants.summary: One pointer walks each sorted input; the smaller item goes next.
variants.requires: Both inputs are sorted the same way.

variants.name: From the middle out
variants.summary: Start at a centre and widen both ends while a condition holds.
variants.requires: The property can be checked by growing outward one step at a time.

visual.caption: Each comparison rules out one end for good. The answer, if there is one, stays between the pointers.
